title: Morning inbox triage into labeled queues
summary: Each morning SI sorts the shared inbox into clear queues, flags what is urgent, and leaves draft replies for a person to review.
problem: A shared inbox mixes customer questions, vendor mail, invoices, newsletters and spam. Urgent messages get buried, and the first hour of the day goes to figuring out what needs attention instead of answering it.
what_si_does: SI reads new messages, applies labels you define (for example: new request, existing customer, billing, vendor, needs owner, ignore), and pulls out the key detail for each, such as a job address, an account name or a requested date. It marks anything time-sensitive, writes a short summary at the top of each queue and leaves draft replies for routine questions. Nothing goes out without a person pressing send.
setup: Connect the inbox with permission to read, label and draft, but not send. Write down your queue names, what counts as urgent, and a handful of good past replies to match your tone. Setup is often a few days, followed by a week or two of adjusting the rules.
human_checks: A person reviews and sends every draft; SI never sends on its own.
Messages SI is unsure about go to a 'needs a human' queue rather than being guessed.
Labels and urgency rules are reviewed after the first couple of weeks and adjusted.

examples.scenario: Overnight emails are split into emergency calls (no heat, active leak), new estimate requests with the address and problem pulled out, and supplier mail, so the dispatcher starts with the emergencies.
During busy season, client emails are labeled by client and topic (missing document, question about a return, payment), and anything mentioning a notice or deadline is flagged for a partner.
Tenant emails are sorted into maintenance, rent and lease questions, and prospective-tenant inquiries, with maintenance messages marked by urgency.

copy_prompt: Go through the unread messages in [inbox] from the last [24 hours]. Label each one as [list of queues]. Mark anything that mentions [urgent terms, e.g. leak, deadline, cancel] as urgent. For each message, write a one-line summary and pull out [key details, e.g. address, account, date]. Draft replies only for messages that match these examples: [paste 3-5 good past replies]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: The day starts with a sorted list instead of a raw inbox, and urgent messages are less likely to sit unseen.

title: A weekly list of emails still waiting on you
summary: Once a week SI finds threads where a customer, client or vendor is still waiting for your reply, and lists them with a suggested next step.
problem: Some emails get read, mentally filed as 'later', and never answered. Nobody notices until the other person follows up, annoyed, or quietly takes their business elsewhere.
what_si_does: SI scans received and sent mail for the past few weeks and finds threads where the last message came from someone else and asked a question or requested something. It skips newsletters, notifications and threads that were clearly closed. The result is a short list grouped by who is waiting, how long they have waited, and what they asked, with a draft reply for the simple ones.
setup: Read access to the mailbox (and draft access if you want replies drafted). A list of senders or domains to ignore. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: A person decides which threads actually need a reply and sends any drafts.
Threads involving complaints or money are flagged for the owner rather than drafted.
The ignore list is updated as false alarms show up.

examples.scenario: Friday afternoon, the principal gets a list of six client and consultant emails with open questions, including a structural engineer waiting on a drawing revision for nine days.
The list shows two clients who asked about adding a driver to their policy and never heard back, plus a carrier underwriter waiting on a signed form.
Three inquiry emails about spring events are surfaced, each with the requested date and headcount, before those dates get booked by someone else.

copy_prompt: Look through my inbox [mailbox] for the last [21] days. Find threads where the most recent message is from someone else and they asked a question or requested something. Ignore [newsletters, notifications, these senders]. List each one with who is waiting, how many days, and what they asked. Draft short replies for the simple ones only. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer people fall through the cracks, and the weekly list makes it easier to close loops before they turn into complaints.

title: Answering 'where is it?' questions from your own records
summary: When a customer asks about the status of an order, job, repair or application, SI looks it up in your system and drafts an accurate reply.
problem: A large share of incoming messages are some version of 'where is my thing?'. Answering each one means opening another system, finding the record and writing the same kind of message again.
what_si_does: SI recognizes status questions, finds the matching record by name, number, address or email, and reads the current state: shipped and tracking number, technician scheduled, part on order, waiting on the customer. It drafts a reply in your tone with the real details, and flags cases where the record looks stuck or contradicts what the customer was told.
setup: Read access to the system that holds status (order system, job management tool, repair log or a shared sheet) and to the inbox or helpdesk. A few example replies and the rules for when a delay should go to a person. Setup is often several days.
human_checks: A person approves each reply until the drafts are consistently right, and can keep approving after that.
Anything that looks stuck or overdue goes to a person with the record attached.
SI does not promise dates that are not in the record.

examples.scenario: A customer emails asking about their dishwasher; SI finds the ticket, sees the part is on backorder with an expected date, and drafts a reply with that date and an offer to call.
A homeowner asks when installation will happen; SI checks the production board, sees the doors are in finishing, and drafts a reply with the current stage and the scheduled install week.
A 'where is my order' email is matched to the order, tracking shows it stalled for five days, and the draft apologizes and offers a replacement option for the owner to approve.

copy_prompt: For each message in [inbox/queue] asking about the status of [an order/job/repair], find the matching record in [system or file] using [order number, name, email or address]. Draft a reply that states the current status and next step using only what is in the record. Flag any record with no update in [5] days. Use this tone: [example reply]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Routine status questions get faster, more accurate answers, and stuck jobs or orders come to light sooner.

title: Refunds, returns and cancellations checked against your policy
summary: SI checks each refund, return, cancellation or reschedule request against your written policy and drafts the answer for approval.
problem: Requests to cancel, return or get money back are handled differently depending on who answers. Some get approved that should not, others get refused that should have been honored, and both lead to friction.
what_si_does: SI reads the request, finds the relevant record (purchase date, booking date, deposit paid, contract terms), and compares it with your written policy. It labels the request as clearly within policy, clearly outside, or a judgment call, and drafts the reply with the reason in plain language. Judgment calls go to the owner with the facts laid out.
setup: Your written policy, read access to the records, and the inbox or form where requests arrive. Setup is often a few days, mostly spent turning an informal policy into clear rules.
human_checks: A person approves every refund, credit or fee waiver; SI never issues money.
Judgment calls and upset customers go to the owner.
The policy document is the source of truth; SI does not invent exceptions.

examples.scenario: A member asks to cancel mid-contract after moving; SI checks the membership terms, finds the relocation clause, and drafts a reply listing the proof needed.
A couple asks to move their date; SI checks the contract's change terms and deposit rules and drafts options for the manager to choose between.
A return request arrives 40 days after delivery; SI notes it is outside the 30-day window but the item was delivered damaged, and marks it as a judgment call.

copy_prompt: Here is my policy for [refunds/returns/cancellations]: [paste]. For each request in [inbox/form], find the record in [system/file], and decide whether it is within policy, outside policy, or a judgment call. Draft a reply that explains the decision in plain language. List judgment calls separately with the facts. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Requests get consistent answers, and the owner only sees the cases that need a real decision.

title: Building an FAQ from answers you have already written
summary: SI reads past replies to customers, groups the questions that keep coming up, and drafts a plain FAQ or help page for you to edit.
problem: The same questions arrive every week, and the best answers are scattered across old emails written by different people. New staff reinvent answers, and customers cannot find them on their own.
what_si_does: SI goes through a few months of sent replies, groups similar questions, picks the clearest past answer for each, and rewrites it into a short FAQ entry. It notes where past answers disagreed so you can decide which is right, and lists questions that may deserve a policy rather than an answer.
setup: An export of a few months of replies or read access to the helpdesk. Setup is often a few days, then editing time on your side.
human_checks: The owner approves every answer before it is published.
Conflicting past answers are resolved by a person.
Anything involving prices, guarantees or legal terms is double-checked.

examples.scenario: Past emails produce entries on vaccine schedules, what to bring to a first visit, and after-hours emergency options, ready for the front desk to review.
Questions about access hours, unit sizes, insurance and move-out notice become a single page staff can link to.
Repeated client questions about support hours, change requests and billing become an onboarding FAQ sent with every new contract.

copy_prompt: Read these past replies [export or folder]. Group the questions that come up more than [3] times. For each group, write a short FAQ entry using the clearest past answer, in plain language. List any groups where past answers disagree. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer repeat questions, faster onboarding of new staff, and answers that match from person to person.

title: Replies to online reviews and public comments
summary: SI watches reviews, comments and messages on your public pages, flags the ones worth answering, and drafts replies in your voice.
problem: Reviews and comments arrive on several platforms, and answering them slips. Negative reviews sit unanswered for weeks, and genuine questions in comments get lost among the noise.
what_si_does: SI collects new reviews and comments, sorts them into praise, question, complaint and spam, and drafts short replies for the ones that need one. Complaints get a careful, non-defensive draft with an offer to take the conversation offline, and are flagged for the owner. It never argues or reveals private details.
setup: Access or exports from the review and social platforms you use, plus a few examples of replies you like. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: Every public reply is approved by a person before posting.
Complaints and anything mentioning safety, injury or legal threats go straight to the owner.
Replies never include private customer details.

examples.scenario: A two-star review about a long wait gets a calm draft that acknowledges the night, without excuses, and invites the guest to contact the manager.
Questions in social comments about insurance claims are flagged with a draft pointing people to call for an estimate.
Positive reviews get short thank-you drafts that avoid confirming the reviewer is a patient.

copy_prompt: Here are new reviews and comments from [platforms] since [date]: [paste or export]. Sort them into praise, question, complaint and spam. Draft a reply for each praise, question and complaint in this tone: [examples]. Keep complaints calm, short and offer to continue privately. Do not mention any personal details. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Reviews and comments get answered more consistently, and the owner sees complaints early.
caution: Medical, dental and other health practices should never confirm someone is a patient or discuss care in a public reply. Keep replies generic and check privacy rules that apply to you.

title: A website or messaging chat assistant that hands hard cases to a person
summary: SI answers common questions in chat from your own website and documents, and passes anything unusual to a person with the conversation attached.
problem: People ask the same questions in chat or messaging apps at all hours. Either someone answers late, or the chat widget is a form that just says 'we will get back to you'.
what_si_does: SI answers from an approved set of sources: your website, FAQ, price list and policies. It can collect details for a quote or booking request. When a question falls outside its sources, involves a complaint, or the person asks for a human, it stops, says someone will follow up, and sends the conversation summary to staff.
setup: An approved knowledge source, the chat or messaging tool, and clear rules for handoff. Setup is often one to two weeks including testing with real questions.
human_checks: SI answers only from approved sources and says so when it does not know.
Anything involving money, complaints or exceptions is handed to a person.
Staff review a sample of conversations each week and correct answers.

examples.scenario: A visitor asks whether spring cleanups are still available in their town; SI confirms the service area, collects the address and yard size, and sends the request to the office.
SI answers questions about office hours, consultation fees and what documents to bring, and hands any question about a specific case to staff.
SI explains class levels and start dates and collects placement-test requests.

copy_prompt: Using only these sources [website pages, FAQ, price list], answer customer questions in [chat/WhatsApp]. If a question is not covered, involves a complaint or money, or the person asks for a human, say that someone will follow up within [time] and send a summary to [staff contact]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Common questions get answered when the office is closed, and staff pick up the conversations that need them with context in hand.
caution: Law, medical and financial offices: the assistant should share general office information only and never anything that reads as advice on a specific situation.

title: After-hours and busy-time phone coverage
summary: A voice assistant answers calls you would miss, handles common questions, takes detailed messages or requests, and sends staff a summary.
problem: Calls that go to voicemail often never call back. Small offices cannot staff the phone through lunch, evenings and weekends, and busy moments mean the person on the phone cannot also serve the person in front of them.
what_si_does: When nobody picks up, a voice assistant answers with your greeting, handles a short list of approved questions (hours, location, services, how to book), and takes a structured message: name, number, reason, urgency. For true emergencies it follows your escalation rule, such as forwarding to the on-call phone. Staff get a text or email summary of each call.
setup: A phone number or forwarding rule, the approved question list, your escalation rules, and a message format. Setup is often one to two weeks including test calls.
human_checks: Callers are told they are speaking with an automated assistant.
Emergency rules are tested before going live and reviewed regularly.
Staff return every message; the assistant does not make commitments on price or timing beyond what you approved.

examples.scenario: A 9 p.m. no-heat call is identified as urgent and forwarded to the on-call technician, while a request for a maintenance quote becomes a message for the morning.
Over lunch the assistant gives office hours and directions and takes callback messages, routing anything that sounds urgent to the instructions you approved.
After hours, callers' location and vehicle details are collected and texted to the driver on duty.

copy_prompt: Draft a phone script for after-hours calls to [business]. It should greet callers, say it is an automated assistant, answer only these questions [list], take a message with name, number, reason and urgency, and treat these situations as emergencies [list] by [forwarding to number]. Write the summary text staff will receive. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer missed calls turn into lost customers, and staff start the day with clear messages instead of voicemails.
caution: Call recording and automated calls are regulated, and consent rules differ by state and country. Disclose the assistant and any recording, and check the rules that apply before going live. Medical practices should keep the assistant away from clinical questions.

title: Follow-ups for quotes and estimates that went quiet
summary: SI finds quotes and estimates with no reply after a set number of days and drafts a short, specific follow-up for each one.
problem: Quotes go out and then nothing happens. Following up feels awkward and gets skipped, so work is lost to whoever simply called back.
what_si_does: SI checks your quotes or estimates for ones still open after a set period, reads what was quoted and any notes, and drafts a short follow-up that refers to the actual job. It suggests a different angle on the second follow-up (a question, a scheduling option) and marks quotes to close out after the last attempt.
setup: Read access to where quotes live (estimating tool, CRM, accounting system or a folder of PDFs) and draft access to email. Your follow-up timing. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A person approves each follow-up before it is sent.
Quotes the owner wants to handle personally are excluded.
Nothing is discounted or changed without the owner's decision.

examples.scenario: Twelve estimates from the last month are open; each gets a draft that mentions the roof type and the crew's next opening in that neighborhood.
A quote for event banners has had no reply for a week; the draft asks whether the event date is still on and notes the latest order date for delivery in time.
Prospects who received a monthly-service proposal get a follow-up offering a short call to walk through the scope.

copy_prompt: Here are open quotes [file/export] with date sent, customer, job and amount. For each quote older than [7] days with no reply, draft a short follow-up that mentions the specific job and offers [a next step]. For quotes already followed up [2] times, suggest closing them. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: More quotes get a timely follow-up, and the pipeline reflects what is really still open.

title: Turning form and email inquiries into clean CRM records
summary: SI reads each new inquiry from forms and email, creates or updates the CRM contact, and logs what they want and the next step.
problem: Leads arrive through web forms, email, phone messages and referrals. Some get entered twice, some never get entered, and the notes are too thin to follow up well.
what_si_does: SI reads each inquiry, checks for an existing contact to avoid duplicates, and fills in the record: name, company, contact details, what they asked for, budget or timing if mentioned, and how they found you. It assigns the lead by your rules and drafts the first reply or creates the follow-up task.
setup: Write access to the CRM limited to contacts, deals and tasks, plus the form tool and inbox. Your assignment rules. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: Someone reviews new records daily at first, then spot-checks.
First replies are approved before sending.
Merging suspected duplicates is confirmed by a person.

examples.scenario: A contact-form inquiry with date, venue and guest count becomes a lead with the date checked against the calendar and a draft reply with packages.
An email asking for nightly cleaning of a 6,000 square foot office is logged with size, frequency and location, and assigned to the estimator for a walkthrough.
Web inquiries are logged with the type of matter and referral source, and a conflict-check task is created before anyone replies.

copy_prompt: For each new inquiry in [form/inbox], check [CRM] for an existing contact by email and phone. Create or update the contact with name, company, what they need, timing, budget if stated and source. Assign using [rules]. Draft a first reply using [template]. List any possible duplicates for me to confirm. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Leads are logged consistently and the first response goes out sooner, with better notes for whoever follows up.

title: Call notes into a follow-up email and tasks
summary: After a sales or client call, SI turns your notes or the transcript into a recap email, CRM updates and dated tasks.
problem: After a call, the follow-up email and the CRM update are the first things to slip. Details are forgotten, and promised next steps happen late or not at all.
what_si_does: From typed notes, a voice memo or a call transcript, SI writes a short recap: what the client needs, what was agreed, open questions and who does what by when. It drafts the follow-up email, updates the CRM fields and creates tasks with due dates.
setup: A way to get notes or transcripts to SI, and access to the CRM and email drafts. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: The person who was on the call reviews the recap and email before sending.
Pricing or commitments in the recap are checked against what was actually said.
Recording only happens with the consent required where you operate.

examples.scenario: A discovery call transcript becomes a recap listing the client's goals, the two campaigns discussed and a promise to send a proposal by Thursday, with a task created for it.
A rep's voice memo from a site visit becomes notes on roof orientation and the homeowner's financing question, plus a follow-up email with the requested information.
Notes from a call with a medical office about backups become a task list and an email confirming the next meeting.

copy_prompt: Here are my notes or transcript from a call with [client]: [paste]. Write a recap with needs, decisions, open questions and next steps with owners and dates. Draft a follow-up email in my voice. List the CRM fields to update and tasks to create. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Follow-ups go out while the call is fresh, and the CRM reflects what was actually agreed.
caution: Call recording: consent rules differ by state and country, and some require every party to agree. Tell participants and follow the stricter rule if unsure.

title: First-draft proposals from discovery notes
summary: SI turns discovery notes and your past proposals into a structured first draft with scope, timeline and pricing options for you to edit.
problem: Proposals take hours to write and often start from a copy of an old one, with leftover details from another client. The delay means the prospect waits while interest cools.
what_si_does: SI reads the discovery notes and a few of your past proposals, then drafts a proposal in your usual structure: the client's situation in their words, scope, what is not included, timeline, pricing options from your rate sheet, and next steps. It highlights any section where it lacked information instead of guessing.
setup: Your proposal template, a rate sheet, and two or three good past proposals. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: The owner reviews scope and pricing line by line.
SI does not invent pricing; it uses the rate sheet and flags gaps.
Nothing is sent to the prospect without approval.

examples.scenario: Notes from a walkthrough become a proposal with demolition, plumbing and tile scope, an allowance line for fixtures, and a flag that cabinet sizes are still unknown.
A discovery call becomes a proposal with three package options and a timeline built from the studio's standard phases.
Notes from a meeting with a 40-person company become a proposal outline with the review steps and a section marked for the consultant to fill in.

copy_prompt: Using these discovery notes [paste], my template [file], rate sheet [file] and these past proposals [files], draft a proposal for [client]. Include situation, scope, exclusions, timeline, [2-3] pricing options and next steps. Mark any section where information is missing. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Proposals go out sooner and start from a clean, client-specific draft instead of a recycled one.

title: A one-page brief on a prospect before you meet
summary: Before a meeting or pitch, SI gathers public information about the organization and your past contact into a short brief.
problem: Walking into a meeting unprepared costs credibility, but researching every prospect takes time nobody has. Past emails and notes about the account are scattered.
what_si_does: SI reads the prospect's website, recent public news and any public profiles you point it to, plus your own CRM notes and past emails. It produces a one-page brief: what they do, size and locations if public, recent changes, who you are meeting, past interactions, and three questions worth asking. Sources are listed so you can check them.
setup: Read access to your CRM and email, plus a list of sources you consider acceptable. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: The person meeting the prospect checks facts against the listed sources.
SI uses public and your own information only.
Anything uncertain is marked as such, not stated as fact.

examples.scenario: Before meeting a growing restaurant group, the brief notes the two new locations opening, the current carrier mentioned in an old email, and questions about liquor liability.
A brief on a regional manufacturer covers its open job postings, recent plant expansion news, and the last conversation with its HR manager.
Before a school district interview, the brief summarizes the district's published facilities plan and past projects of similar size.

copy_prompt: Prepare a one-page brief on [organization] for a meeting on [date] with [names]. Use their website [URL], these public sources [list], and my CRM notes and emails about them. Include what they do, recent changes, who I am meeting, past contact with us, and [3] good questions. List sources for every fact. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Meetings start better prepared, with less last-minute scrambling.

title: Personal outreach drafts and reply handling you approve
summary: SI drafts first-touch and follow-up messages from real research, sorts the replies, and offers meeting times, with every message approved by you.
problem: Generic outreach gets ignored, and personal outreach takes too long to write. Replies, when they come, sit unsorted while interested people go cold.
what_si_does: From a list of prospects and a short brief on each, SI drafts a short first message that refers to something specific and relevant, plus one or two follow-ups. When replies come in, it sorts them into interested, not now, wrong person and no, drafts an answer for each, and proposes open times from your calendar for the interested ones. Unsubscribe and no-contact requests are recorded and respected.
setup: Your prospect list, calendar access, and a clear description of what you offer. Setup is often several days.
human_checks: Every message is approved before sending, and volume stays modest.
Opt-outs are honored immediately and recorded.
Outreach follows the anti-spam and privacy rules that apply to you.

examples.scenario: Drafts to office managers at nearby firms mention their recent move into a new building and offer a tasting; replies asking for menus get a draft with the menu and two tasting times.
Property managers of older buildings get a note about seasonal maintenance; a 'not now, try in spring' reply becomes a dated reminder.
Small nonprofits with an upcoming grant cycle get a short note offering a review of last year's application.

copy_prompt: For each prospect in [list] with these notes [research], draft a first message of under [100] words that mentions one specific, relevant detail and offers [offer]. Draft [2] short follow-ups. Then sort these replies [paste] into interested, not now, wrong person and no, and draft an answer for each, offering times from [calendar]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Outreach becomes more personal without taking all afternoon, and interested replies get answered quickly.
caution: Outbound email and messaging are regulated (for example CAN-SPAM in the US and stricter rules in the EU and Canada). Include opt-out handling and follow the rules that apply to you.

title: Check-ins for repeat customers who are due
summary: SI spots regular customers who are past their usual reorder or rebooking interval and drafts a friendly, specific check-in.
problem: Repeat customers are the easiest business to keep, but nobody tracks when each one is due. They drift away quietly, or simply buy from whoever reached out first.
what_si_does: SI reads your order, invoice or appointment history, works out each regular customer's usual interval, and lists those who are overdue. For each, it drafts a short check-in that mentions what they usually order or book and offers an easy next step.
setup: An export of order, invoice or booking history and draft access to email or text. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A person reviews the list and approves each message.
Customers who asked not to be contacted are excluded.
Customers with open complaints or unpaid balances are flagged instead of nudged.

examples.scenario: A cafe that orders every two weeks has not ordered in four; the draft mentions their usual blend and asks whether anything changed.
Customers who booked an opening last spring but not this spring get a reminder with open dates.
Clients who usually book every six weeks and are now at nine get a text draft offering their stylist's next openings.

copy_prompt: Using this order or booking history [file], find each customer's usual interval between [orders/visits]. List customers who are more than [50%] past their usual interval, with their last date and usual purchase. Draft a short check-in for each in this tone: [example]. Exclude [do-not-contact list]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Regular customers hear from you before they drift, and the outreach feels personal rather than mass-mailed.

title: Supplier invoices from email into draft bills
summary: SI reads supplier invoices that arrive by email, creates draft bills in your accounting tool, and flags duplicates or missing details.
problem: Invoices arrive as PDFs in several inboxes. Someone retypes them into the accounting system, and duplicates, typos and missed due dates follow.
what_si_does: SI watches an invoices inbox, reads each attachment, and extracts supplier, invoice number, date, due date, line totals and tax. It creates a draft bill with a suggested account based on past coding, and checks for problems: an invoice number already entered, an amount that does not match the purchase order, missing tax registration details, or a changed bank account on the invoice.
setup: A dedicated invoices inbox or forwarding rule, accounting access limited to creating drafts, and your past coding as a reference. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: The bookkeeper reviews and approves each draft bill.
SI never pays bills or changes supplier bank details.
A change in a supplier's payment details is always flagged and confirmed by phone with a known contact.

examples.scenario: Lumber and electrical supply invoices are turned into draft bills tagged to the right job, and a second copy of the same invoice sent by a supplier's rep is caught.
Weekly produce, meat and linen invoices become draft bills with food and non-food costs coded separately.
Vendor invoices for repairs are matched to the property and unit, and one arriving with new bank details is flagged before anyone pays it.

copy_prompt: Read the invoices in [inbox/folder] from [date]. For each, extract supplier, invoice number, dates, totals and tax. Suggest an account using this past coding [file]. Flag duplicates (same supplier and number or amount), missing details, mismatches with [PO file], and any change in payment details. Prepare draft bills only. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Less retyping, fewer duplicate payments, and payment-detail changes get a second look.

title: Matching receipts to card transactions
summary: SI matches receipts from email and photos to card transactions, suggests categories, and lists what is still missing before month end.
problem: Card transactions pile up without receipts. At month end someone hunts through email and phone photos to match them, and expense reports are late.
what_si_does: SI reads receipts from a forwarding inbox or shared folder, matches them to transactions by amount, date and merchant, suggests a category from past coding, and builds a missing-receipts list per cardholder. It can also assemble a simple expense report for staff who pay out of pocket.
setup: Card transaction feed or export, a receipts inbox or folder, and the chart of accounts. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: The bookkeeper confirms categories before anything is posted.
Reminders to cardholders about missing receipts are reviewed before sending.
Unusual or personal-looking charges are flagged for the owner.

examples.scenario: Fuel and hardware-store receipts snapped by field crews are matched to the company cards, and each crew lead gets a short list of what is missing.
Travel receipts from a client trip are matched and grouped into an expense report ready to be billed back to the client.
Program staff purchases are matched and coded to the right grant so grant reports are easier at quarter end.

copy_prompt: Match these card transactions [export] to the receipts in [folder/inbox]. Match on amount, date (within [3] days) and merchant. Suggest a category using this past coding [file]. List unmatched transactions by cardholder, and flag anything unusual. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Month end has fewer surprises, and chasing receipts becomes a short list instead of a search.

title: Reminders for overdue invoices, firmer as they age
summary: SI checks open invoices each week and drafts reminders whose tone matches how late each one is, for you to approve.
problem: Chasing money is uncomfortable, so it gets put off. Invoices drift from 30 to 90 days late, and by then the conversation is harder.
what_si_does: SI reads open invoices and payment history, groups them by how overdue they are, and drafts a reminder for each: a friendly note just after the due date, a clearer one later, and a firm one with next steps after that, using your terms. It skips customers with a payment plan or a dispute and flags long-overdue accounts for a phone call.
setup: Read access to invoices in your accounting tool and draft access to email. Your reminder schedule and terms. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: A person approves every reminder.
Disputed invoices, payment plans and key accounts are excluded or handled personally.
SI never threatens action; any collections step is the owner's decision.

examples.scenario: Three clients are a week past due and get friendly reminders with the invoice attached; one 60 days late is flagged for the owner to call.
Patient balances after insurance get courteous statement reminders, with any account showing a pending insurance appeal excluded.
Corporate clients get reminders addressed to their accounts-payable contact with the purchase order number included.

copy_prompt: Here are open invoices [export] with customer, amount, due date and notes. Group them by days overdue: [1-14], [15-45], [46+]. Draft a reminder for each group in increasing firmness, using my terms [paste]. Exclude anything marked disputed or on a plan. List accounts over [60] days for a phone call. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Reminders go out on time without the owner having to write them, and the hardest cases get personal attention.
caution: Medical and dental practices: patient billing messages must follow health-privacy rules. Debt collection is also regulated; keep reminders factual and leave collections decisions to the owner.

title: Finding work that was done but never invoiced
summary: SI compares completed jobs, time entries or deliveries against invoices sent and lists anything that was never billed.
problem: Small jobs, extra hours and change orders get done and then forgotten at billing time. Nobody notices the gap because nothing looks wrong.
what_si_does: SI lines up the record of work done (closed job tickets, timesheets, delivery notes, change orders) against invoices issued. It lists items with no matching invoice, partial billing, or hours logged above what was billed, and prepares draft invoices or a list for the billing person.
setup: Read access to the job, time or delivery system and to invoicing. Setup is often a few days, mostly agreeing on how to match records.
human_checks: The owner or billing person confirms each item before any invoice is drafted or sent.
Work done as a courtesy or under warranty is marked so it is not flagged again.
Customer-facing invoices are approved before sending.

examples.scenario: A closed ticket for a water heater flush and two change orders on a bathroom job have no invoice; drafts are prepared for the office manager.
Logged hours on a matter exceed what was billed last month, and the gap is listed for the billing partner to review.
Rental extensions recorded at return were never added to the customer's invoice.

copy_prompt: Compare these completed jobs or time entries [export] with these invoices [export] for [period]. Match on [job number, client, date]. List work with no invoice, partial invoices, and hours logged above hours billed. Draft invoices only for items I confirm. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Less revenue slips away unnoticed, and billing reviews have something concrete to check.

title: Month-end close prep and the accountant's package
summary: SI prepares the month-end checklist, reconciliation exceptions and an indexed bundle of documents for the bookkeeper or accountant.
problem: Month end means chasing missing documents, explaining odd transactions and emailing files back and forth. It drags on, and the accountant's questions arrive weeks later.
what_si_does: SI runs through your close checklist: unreconciled bank lines with suggested matches, uncategorized transactions with suggested categories, missing receipts and bills, and balances that moved oddly from last month. It writes a short note on each exception and gathers the month's statements, invoices and receipts into one indexed folder for the accountant.
setup: Read access to the accounting tool, bank exports and document folders. Your checklist. Setup is often about a week.
human_checks: The bookkeeper or accountant reviews every proposed match and category.
SI does not post journal entries.
The package is reviewed before it is shared.

examples.scenario: The package includes bank and card statements, supplier invoices, and a note that lab fees are unusually high this month because of a batch of crowns.
Unreconciled lines include two customer deposits with suggested invoice matches, and a raw-materials bill with no receiving record.
Payment-processor payouts are broken into sales, fees and refunds so they reconcile against the bank deposits.

copy_prompt: For [month], go through my close checklist [paste]. List unreconciled bank lines with suggested matches, uncategorized transactions with suggested categories, missing receipts or bills, and balances that changed by more than [20%] from last month, with a short note on each. Gather statements and documents from [folders] into one indexed folder for the accountant. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Close tends to finish sooner, with fewer rounds of questions from the accountant.

title: Tracking subscriptions, contracts and renewal dates
summary: SI finds recurring charges and contract renewal dates in statements and documents, and warns you before anything auto-renews.
problem: Software subscriptions, service contracts, leases and insurance policies renew automatically. Nobody remembers what each one costs, whether it is still used, or when the notice period starts.
what_si_does: SI scans card and bank statements for recurring charges and reads contracts for term, renewal and notice dates. It builds one list with cost, owner, renewal date and notice deadline, highlights duplicates and tools nobody seems to use, and sends a reminder well before each notice deadline.
setup: Statement exports and a folder of contracts. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A person decides what to cancel or renegotiate; SI never cancels anything.
Contract dates SI extracts are checked against the document.
Reminders go to the named owner of each contract.

examples.scenario: The list shows two overlapping document-sharing tools and a tax software license that renews just before busy season.
Elevator maintenance, landscaping and insurance contracts across buildings are listed with notice deadlines, so renegotiation starts in time.
Seats for former staff on several design and project tools are flagged.

copy_prompt: Review these statements [files] for recurring charges, and these contracts [folder] for term, renewal and notice dates. Build one list with vendor, cost, frequency, owner, renewal date and notice deadline. Flag duplicates and anything with no clear owner. Set reminders [30] days before each notice deadline. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer surprise renewals, and unused tools get noticed.
caution: Contract dates and terms pulled by SI are a starting point, not a legal reading. Check the actual document, and ask a lawyer about anything unclear.

title: A year-end document packet for your tax preparer
summary: SI sorts the year's documents, totals them by category and flags gaps, so your tax preparer gets one organized packet.
problem: At tax time, documents are spread across email, folders and paper. The preparer sends a list of questions, and gathering the answers takes weeks.
what_si_does: SI goes through the year's folders and inbox for tax-related documents: income forms, statements, receipts, vehicle and home-office records, donation receipts and prior-year notices. It sorts and renames them, builds an index and category totals, and lists what seems to be missing compared with last year's packet. It does not decide what is deductible.
setup: Access to the relevant folders and inbox, last year's packet or the preparer's checklist. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: The owner and tax preparer review the packet; SI makes no tax judgments.
Sensitive documents are shared only through the preparer's secure channel.
Category totals are checked against source documents.

examples.scenario: Supply receipts, vehicle mileage logs and 1099s from three general contractors are organized, with a note that one 1099 from last year's client has not arrived.
Payroll summaries, sales tax filings and equipment purchase invoices are gathered for the accountant's checklist.
Repair invoices, insurance and property tax bills are sorted by property.

copy_prompt: Using [folders/inbox], find tax-related documents for [year]. Sort and rename them by [category], build an index and category totals, and compare against this checklist [preparer's list or last year's packet] to list what is missing. Do not decide what is deductible. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Tax prep starts organized, and the back-and-forth with the preparer tends to be shorter.
caution: Tax: SI organizes documents and drafts summaries; it does not give tax advice or decide what is deductible. A qualified accountant or tax preparer makes those calls.

title: A one-page weekly snapshot for the owner
summary: Every Monday, SI pulls the numbers you care about from your tools into a single page with short notes on what changed.
problem: The numbers that matter live in five different systems. Checking them takes a morning, so it does not happen regularly, and problems show up late.
what_si_does: SI collects a short, fixed set of measures each week (for example sales, new inquiries, jobs completed, cash in the bank, overdue invoices, open complaints) and lays them out against last week and the same week last year. It adds a few plain sentences on what moved and why, where the data shows it.
setup: Read access to the tools involved and an agreed list of no more than about ten measures. Setup is often about a week.
human_checks: The owner chooses the measures and checks the first few reports against the source systems.
Explanations are marked as likely causes, not certainties.
Access is read-only.

examples.scenario: The page shows car count, average repair order and comebacks by location, with a note that one shop's car count dropped during a week a technician was out.
Partners see returns in progress, returns waiting on clients, billed hours and unpaid invoices each Monday in tax season.
Sales by location and day, food cost from supplier bills, and weather notes on slow days.

copy_prompt: Every [Monday], pull these measures [list] from [tools] for last week. Show each against the prior week and the same week last year. Write [3-5] plain sentences on what changed and the likely reasons visible in the data, marked as likely. Keep it to one page. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: The owner sees the business at a glance every week, and changes get noticed while they are still small.

title: One view of revenue across every place you take money
summary: SI combines sales from each channel, location or payment system into one sheet or dashboard that updates on a schedule.
problem: Money comes in through a point-of-sale system, online payments, invoices and maybe a marketplace or two. Each has its own report, and none of them agree on the total.
what_si_does: SI pulls sales from each source, maps them to common categories (location, product or service line, channel), removes double-counting such as an invoice also recorded as a card payment, and keeps one table and a simple dashboard current. It notes where sources disagree.
setup: Read access or regular exports from each source and an agreed set of categories. Setup is often one to two weeks.
human_checks: Totals are checked against the accounting system each month.
Category mapping is reviewed by the owner.
Discrepancies are reported, not quietly adjusted.

examples.scenario: Taproom sales, distributor invoices and online merchandise sales appear together by week and by product.
Lesson payments, recital ticket sales and instrument rentals are combined, with family accounts paid by both card and check de-duplicated.
In-store sales, online orders and a marketplace channel are combined by product category so slow lines are visible across all three.

copy_prompt: Combine sales from these sources [exports or connections] for [period]. Map each to these categories [location, line, channel]. Remove double-counted payments by matching [invoice number, amount and date]. Build one table and a simple chart by [week]. List any discrepancies between sources. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: One trusted number for revenue, and a clear picture of which channels or lines are growing.

title: Plain-language notes when a number moves
summary: When a key number jumps or drops, SI looks for likely reasons in the data and writes a short, plain note for the owner.
problem: Dashboards show that something changed but not why. Someone has to dig through reports to find out, and often nobody does.
what_si_does: SI watches a few chosen measures. When one moves past a threshold you set, it checks the obvious breakdowns (by location, product, customer, staff member, channel, day) and writes a short note: what changed, where the change is concentrated, and what to look at next. It presents causes as possibilities.
setup: Read access to the underlying data and thresholds for each measure. Setup is often several days.
human_checks: Notes are labeled as possible explanations for a person to confirm.
Thresholds are adjusted to avoid noise.
No action is taken automatically.

examples.scenario: New-client visits dropped noticeably this month; the note shows the drop is almost entirely from one referral source that stopped sending patients.
Food cost rose at one location; the note points to a price increase on one supplier's invoices and a menu item selling more than usual.
Monthly online donations fell; the note shows recurring donors whose cards expired.

copy_prompt: Watch these measures [list] in [data source]. When one changes by more than [threshold] versus [comparison period], break it down by [dimensions] and write a short note on where the change is concentrated and what to check next. Present causes as possibilities. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Changes get explained sooner, and the owner spends less time digging through reports.

title: Ad spend next to real results, in one sheet
summary: SI lines up spend from each ad platform with the inquiries, bookings or sales it produced, and lists campaigns that look weak.
problem: Each ad platform reports its own success, often generously. Comparing spend with actual customers means stitching exports together by hand.
what_si_does: SI pulls spend by campaign from each platform and matches it to results in your own systems (form leads, booked calls, sales by source or promo code). It shows cost per lead or sale by campaign and week, and lists campaigns with spend but little real result, with suggestions to review.
setup: Read access or exports from the ad platforms and your lead or sales system, plus consistent tracking such as source fields or codes. Setup is often about a week.
human_checks: Budget changes are made by a person; SI only recommends.
Attribution gaps are stated plainly.
Recommendations are reviewed with whoever runs the ads.

examples.scenario: Search ad spend by campaign is matched to signed intake forms rather than clicks, showing which campaigns bring qualified calls.
Social ads in two towns produce plenty of leads but few booked cleanings; the sheet lists them for review.
Spend by campaign is compared with orders using the store's source tracking, alongside the platforms' own numbers.

copy_prompt: Combine ad spend by campaign and week from [platforms/exports] with results from [lead or sales system] matched by [source, campaign tag or code]. Show cost per [lead/booking/sale] by campaign. List campaigns with spend above [amount] and few results, with suggestions. Note any gaps in tracking. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Ad decisions rest on real customers, and weak campaigns are easier to spot.
caution: Law firms and health practices: advertising is subject to professional and privacy rules, and tracking tools must not send protected client or patient information to ad platforms.

title: A weekly watch on competitors' prices and offers
summary: Once a week SI checks the competitor pages you choose and sends a short summary of changed prices, services, offers or openings.
problem: Owners know competitors matter but rarely have time to check their sites. Price changes and new offers are noticed months later, usually from a customer.
what_si_does: SI visits a fixed list of public competitor pages (pricing, menus, service lists, promotions, job postings) and compares them with last week's snapshot. It records changes in a sheet and sends a short summary of what is new, with links.
setup: A list of competitors and pages to watch. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: SI only reads public pages and respects site terms.
Pricing decisions remain with the owner.
The watch list is reviewed every few months.

examples.scenario: Two nearby practices started advertising new-patient whitening offers, and one now lists evening hours.
A competitor's posted rates for local moves went up, and another added a storage service.
Event calendars of nearby shops and libraries are tracked so author events do not clash.

copy_prompt: Every [week], check these public pages [list of URLs] and compare them with last week's version. Record changes in prices, services, offers, hours and job postings in [sheet]. Send me a short summary with links. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Competitor changes are noticed in weeks rather than months.

title: A weekly team report assembled from the tools you already use
summary: SI pulls updates from project, support and sales tools into a draft weekly report that a manager edits and sends.
problem: Writing the weekly update means asking everyone for status and copying from several tools. It takes a manager's afternoon, and the result is often late or thin.
what_si_does: SI reads what changed during the week: tasks completed and overdue in the project tool, tickets opened and closed, deals moved, and notes from team channels. It drafts a report with highlights, risks, overdue items and decisions needed, in the format your team already uses.
setup: Read access to the tools involved and an example of a good past report. Setup is often several days.
human_checks: The manager edits and sends the report.
Risks and personnel matters are worded by a person.
SI does not post to shared channels without approval.

examples.scenario: The Friday report lists each job's progress, inspections passed or pending, change orders, and material delays from supplier emails.
Client projects are summarized with deliverables shipped, items waiting on clients, and hours used against budget.
Volunteer hours, events held and grant deliverables due next month are rolled into the director's update.

copy_prompt: Read this week's activity in [project tool, helpdesk, CRM, channels]. Draft a weekly report in this format [example] with highlights, risks, overdue items and decisions needed. Keep it under [one page]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Reports go out on time with less effort, and overdue items are visible to everyone.

title: Monthly themes from customer questions, complaints and surveys
summary: SI groups a month of support messages, reviews and survey answers by theme, counts them, and suggests what to fix upstream.
problem: The same problems generate complaints month after month, but nobody steps back to count them. Fixes target whatever was loudest, not what was most common.
what_si_does: SI reads the month's tickets, emails, reviews and survey comments, groups them by underlying cause (billing confusion, late arrivals, unclear instructions, a product defect), counts each, and quotes a few representative examples. It suggests one or two upstream fixes for the biggest themes.
setup: Exports from the helpdesk, review sites or survey tool. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: The owner decides which themes to act on.
Personal details are removed from quoted examples.
Theme groupings are checked against a sample of raw messages.

examples.scenario: Many calls this month were about how to read the new online lab results, suggesting a short guide for parents.
Complaints group into arrival-window misses and surprise charges for stairs, pointing to clearer quotes.
End-of-course evaluations show repeated requests for evening sections and earlier access to materials.

copy_prompt: Here are this month's support messages, reviews and survey comments [exports]. Group them by underlying cause, count each group, and quote [2] representative examples with personal details removed. Suggest [1-2] upstream fixes for the largest groups. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Recurring problems become visible and countable, which makes it easier to fix them at the source.

title: Drafting next week's staff schedule from availability
summary: SI collects availability and time-off requests and drafts next week's schedule against your coverage rules, for a manager to adjust.
problem: Building the schedule means reconciling texts, time-off requests, availability changes and coverage needs. It eats a manager's evening and still leaves gaps.
what_si_does: SI gathers availability and requests from a form or shared sheet, applies your rules (minimum coverage per shift, required skills or certifications, maximum hours, fair rotation of weekends), and drafts a schedule. It lists any shift it could not fill and any rule it had to bend, so the manager decides.
setup: A form or sheet for availability, your coverage rules, and the scheduling tool or sheet. Setup is often several days.
human_checks: The manager reviews and publishes the schedule.
Overtime and rule exceptions are decided by a person.
Labor rules such as required breaks and minors' hours are confirmed by the manager.

examples.scenario: Servers' availability and two time-off requests produce a draft with a trained bartender on every shift, and a Saturday double flagged as overtime.
Caregiver availability is matched against client visit times and travel areas, with one uncovered visit flagged.
Weekend shifts rotate fairly across part-timers, and holiday coverage is drafted a month ahead.

copy_prompt: Using this availability [sheet/form responses] and these time-off requests [list], draft a schedule for [week] that meets these rules [coverage, skills, max hours, rotation]. List unfilled shifts and any rule you could not meet. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Schedules come together faster, and gaps are visible before the week starts.

title: Turning how-we-do-it into written procedures
summary: SI turns a recorded walkthrough, voice memo or screen recording into a clear, step-by-step procedure your team can follow.
problem: Know-how lives in a few people's heads. Training is slow, mistakes repeat, and the business depends on whoever remembers how things are done.
what_si_does: A team member records themselves doing the task, or just talks it through. SI turns the recording or transcript into a numbered procedure with purpose, tools needed, steps, checks, common mistakes and who to ask. It lists steps that seemed unclear so the expert can fill them in.
setup: A way to record (phone, screen recorder, video call) and a shared place for procedures. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: The expert reviews each procedure before it is shared.
Safety-related steps are checked by whoever is responsible for safety.
Procedures are dated and reviewed when processes change.

examples.scenario: The head baker narrates the opening routine, and SI writes a procedure covering oven checks, proofing times and allergen cleaning.
A screen recording of submitting a claim correction becomes a step-by-step guide with screenshots referenced.
The move-out inspection process becomes a checklist with photo requirements per room.

copy_prompt: Here is a transcript or recording of [person] doing [task]: [file]. Write a procedure with purpose, tools needed, numbered steps, checks, common mistakes and who to ask. List any steps that are unclear. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Training gets easier, and the business depends less on one person remembering everything.

title: Appointment confirmations, reminders and reschedules
summary: SI sends approved confirmation and reminder messages, handles reschedule requests against your real calendar, and keeps the schedule current.
problem: No-shows and last-minute changes waste slots. Staff spend time calling to confirm and juggling reschedules over text, email and phone.
what_si_does: SI sends confirmations and reminders from approved templates at set times before each appointment, reads replies, and handles simple reschedules by offering open slots that fit your rules (provider, room, length). Anything unusual, such as a request to change the type of appointment or a complaint, goes to staff.
setup: Calendar or booking-system access, approved templates, and reschedule rules. Setup is often a few days to a week.
human_checks: Templates are approved once by a person, and anything outside them goes to staff.
Cancellations within the fee window are handled by staff.
Messages contain only what the client needs to know.

examples.scenario: Patients get a reminder two days before; a patient who replies that she has a conflict is offered three openings with the same hygienist.
Drop-off confirmations go out the day before, with a note about the shuttle schedule.
Families get reminders, and a reschedule request is matched to the same tutor's open slots.

copy_prompt: Using [calendar/booking system], draft confirmation and reminder messages for appointments [timing, e.g. 48 hours before]. For reschedule replies, offer [3] open slots that match [provider, length, location]. Send anything else to [staff]. Show me the templates and the first day's messages. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer no-shows and less phone tag, with staff handling only the unusual changes.
caution: Medical and dental offices: reminder messages should follow health-privacy rules (for example HIPAA in the US). Keep details minimal and use approved channels.

title: Meeting notes into owners and due dates
summary: SI turns a meeting transcript or rough notes into a short summary, decisions and a task list with owners and due dates.
problem: Meetings end with agreement, then nothing happens because nobody wrote down who would do what. The next meeting starts by rediscussing the last one.
what_si_does: From a transcript or notes, SI writes a short summary, decisions made, open questions and action items with an owner and due date for each. It can post the summary to the team channel and add tasks to the project tool once approved, and starts the next agenda with any items still open.
setup: Access to transcripts or notes, the team channel and the task tool. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: The meeting organizer reviews the summary before it is shared.
Task owners confirm their tasks.
Recording is used only with participants' consent.

examples.scenario: Board meeting notes become draft minutes, a list of motions and votes, and action items for committee chairs.
The weekly site meeting with subcontractors produces a list of who is fixing which punch-list item by when.
The partner meeting's decisions about client assignments are logged and tasks created.

copy_prompt: Here is the transcript or notes from [meeting]: [paste]. Write a short summary, decisions, open questions and action items with owner and due date. Draft a post for [channel] and the tasks for [tool]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Decisions stick, and follow-through is easier to track.
caution: Recording meetings: consent rules vary by place; tell participants and follow the stricter rule if unsure. Formal board minutes should be reviewed by the secretary.

title: Turning meeting requests and forwarded emails into calendar holds
summary: When an email asks to meet or includes a date, SI drafts the reply with real open times and creates a tentative calendar hold for you to confirm.
problem: Scheduling takes several back-and-forth emails, and dates buried in emails, flyers and attachments never make it onto the calendar.
what_si_does: SI reads incoming messages and forwarded items for meeting requests, deadlines and event dates. For meeting requests it checks your calendar and drafts a reply with a few times that fit your rules. For dates in forwarded emails or attachments, it creates tentative events with the details and a link back to the source.
setup: Calendar and email access with draft permissions, plus your scheduling preferences. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: Holds stay tentative until you confirm.
Replies are approved before sending.
SI does not accept invitations on your behalf.

examples.scenario: A buyer's email asking to see two houses on Saturday becomes a draft reply with three time windows and tentative holds.
A forwarded court notice becomes a calendar entry with the hearing date and a reminder a week before.
Dates from a forwarded school newsletter become tentative events on the association's calendar.

copy_prompt: Read [inbox/forwarded messages]. For each meeting request, draft a reply offering [3] times that fit [rules] in my calendar. For each date or deadline mentioned, create a tentative event with the details and a link to the source. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Less back-and-forth to set meetings, and fewer dates fall off the calendar.
caution: Legal deadlines: SI-created entries are a convenience, not a docketing system. Court and filing deadlines must be confirmed by the attorney.

title: A morning briefing across inbox, calendar and tasks
summary: Each morning SI prepares a short briefing on today's meetings, urgent messages, overdue tasks and stalled deals.
problem: Owners start the day reacting to whatever is on top of the inbox. Preparation for meetings happens in the car, and overdue items surface late.
what_si_does: SI reads today's calendar, recent email, the task list and the CRM, and writes a short briefing: meetings with context on each attendee, messages that need a reply today, tasks overdue or due today, and deals or projects with no activity for a while. It is delivered at a set time by email or chat.
setup: Read access to calendar, email, tasks and CRM. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: The briefing is read-only; any follow-up action is approved.
Confidential threads can be excluded.
Content is reviewed after the first week and trimmed to what is useful.

examples.scenario: The briefing lists two commercial bids due this week, a call with a supplier rep, and three customer complaints from yesterday.
Today's donor meeting comes with the donor's giving history and last conversation notes.
Client meetings come with notes from the last review, and the list shows clients who emailed with questions.

copy_prompt: Every morning at [time], read my calendar, email from the last [24 hours], tasks and [CRM]. Write a short briefing: today's meetings with context, messages needing a reply today, overdue tasks, and deals or projects with no activity in [14] days. Send it to [email/chat]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: The day starts with a plan, and meetings start better prepared.

title: Turning incoming work and maintenance requests into scheduled jobs
summary: SI turns work requests from email, forms and messages into job tickets, sorts them by urgency, and drafts a schedule and customer updates.
problem: Requests arrive by phone, text, email and portal. They get written on paper, entered late, or lost, and customers do not know when someone is coming.
what_si_does: SI reads each request, creates a job ticket with the location, problem, urgency and any photos, and checks capacity or vendor availability. It proposes a time slot or the right vendor by your rules, drafts the message to the customer or tenant with the plan, and drafts the dispatch note to the technician or vendor.
setup: Access to the request channels, the job or maintenance system, and your urgency and assignment rules. Setup is often one to two weeks.
human_checks: A dispatcher or manager approves assignments and customer messages.
Emergencies follow your escalation rules and are confirmed by a person.
Vendor work orders above a set amount need approval.

examples.scenario: A tenant's email about a leaking kitchen faucet becomes a ticket marked routine, assigned to the plumbing vendor, with a draft reply giving the expected visit window.
A client's request for an extra floor-waxing visit is scheduled into the next open night crew slot.
Teacher requests for repairs are logged by building and room and grouped into the custodian's weekly plan.

copy_prompt: For each request in [channels], create a ticket with location, problem, urgency per [rules], and attachments. Propose a time or vendor using [capacity calendar or vendor list]. Draft a message to the requester with the plan, and a dispatch note to the assignee. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Requests are captured and acknowledged consistently, and customers know what to expect.

title: Reorder lists from sales pace
summary: On a set schedule, SI turns recent usage or sales and stock on hand into a suggested reorder list grouped by supplier, for you to approve.
problem: Reordering happens from memory or a quick look at the shelf. Fast movers run out, slow movers get reordered anyway, and nobody has time to do the math across hundreds of items.
what_si_does: SI reads recent sales or usage per item, stock on hand and on order, and each supplier's lead time and minimum order. It works out how many days of stock remain, flags anything that will run out before the next delivery could arrive, and drafts a reorder list per supplier with a short reason next to each line (for example, 'using faster than last month, about nine days left, three-week lead time').
setup: Read access to sales or usage data (point of sale, order system, job records or a stock sheet) plus one sheet of suppliers, lead times, pack sizes and minimums. Agree on how much stock to keep per item group. Setup is often about a week including tuning.
human_checks: The buyer or owner reviews every line and edits quantities before anything goes to a supplier.
SI only drafts; it does not place orders.
Seasonal and discontinued items are marked so they are not suggested blindly.

examples.scenario: Weekly usage from the point-of-sale system and the last inventory count produce a list for the produce, dry goods and paper suppliers, with a note that the brunch menu is using eggs faster.
Gloves, impression material and sterilization pouches are tracked from monthly counts, and the order is drafted before the distributor's cutoff.
Units sold per variant over the last 30 and 90 days and current stock produce a reorder list per supplier, flagging three variants that will run out before restock.

copy_prompt: Using this sales or usage data [file] for the last [90] days and my stock on hand [file], estimate days of stock left for each item. Use these lead times and minimums [supplier sheet]. Draft a reorder list grouped by supplier with a one-line reason for each item, and flag anything with less than [14] days left. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Reordering becomes a short review instead of a long spreadsheet session, and shortages on fast movers tend to be caught earlier. Results depend on how clean the lead-time data is.

title: Drafting purchase orders without a dedicated purchasing system
summary: SI turns an approved reorder list into supplier-ready purchase orders in your format, tracks what is open, and drafts the emails.
problem: Many businesses order by phone, text or a quick email with no purchase order. Nobody can say what is on order, what price was agreed or what arrived, especially when a purchasing tool is retired or was never set up.
what_si_does: From an approved list, SI builds a purchase order per supplier with item codes, quantities, agreed prices and delivery address, numbered and saved to a shared folder. It drafts the email to each supplier, keeps an open-orders sheet, and updates it when confirmations or shipping notices arrive.
setup: A purchase order template, supplier list with contacts and item codes, and a shared folder or sheet. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A person approves each purchase order before it is sent.
Price changes on supplier confirmations are flagged.
SI never accepts new terms or changes quantities on its own.

examples.scenario: Materials for two upcoming jobs are combined into one purchase order per supply house, each line tagged to the job.
Orders to five small producers go out as consistent purchase orders, and the open-orders sheet shows which ones have confirmed.
Paper and ink orders are drafted from the reorder list with the distributor's item codes.

copy_prompt: From this approved reorder list [file], create one purchase order per supplier using [template], with PO number, item codes, quantities, agreed prices from [price sheet] and delivery address [address]. Draft the email to each supplier and add each PO to [open-orders sheet]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Ordering becomes traceable: everyone can see what is on order, at what price, and when it is due.

title: Checking deliveries against what was ordered
summary: When a delivery arrives, SI compares the packing slip or invoice with the purchase order and lists shortages, substitutions and price differences.
problem: Deliveries get signed for without a careful count. Shortages, wrong items and price increases are discovered weeks later, after the invoice is paid.
what_si_does: Staff snap a photo of the packing slip or forward the supplier invoice. SI reads it, matches it line by line to the purchase order, and lists anything short, extra, substituted, backordered or priced differently. It drafts a note to the supplier for credits or missing items and updates the open-orders sheet.
setup: Open purchase orders in a sheet or system, and a phone or email path for packing slips. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: Staff confirm physical counts; SI only compares paperwork.
Credit requests are approved before sending.
Invoices with differences are held for review before payment.

examples.scenario: The fish delivery is two kilos short and the produce invoice shows a higher price on lemons; both are flagged before the invoice is entered.
A pallet arrives with a substituted brand of fasteners; the note to the distributor asks for confirmation of price.
A supply order arrives with one item backordered, and the clinic manager is alerted so the item can be sourced elsewhere.

copy_prompt: Compare this packing slip or invoice [photo/PDF] with purchase order [number or file]. List lines that are short, extra, substituted, backordered or priced differently. Draft a note to [supplier] asking for credit or the missing items. Update [open-orders sheet]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Supplier mistakes are caught while they can still be corrected, and invoices are paid for what actually arrived.

title: A daily watch for low stock and stuck orders
summary: Each day SI checks for items running low and orders or jobs that have stalled, and sends a short list with suggested fixes before customers notice.
problem: Problems are found when a customer complains: an item sold that was not in stock, a shipment stuck for a week, a job waiting on a part nobody ordered.
what_si_does: SI checks stock levels against minimums, compares open customer orders or jobs with the stock and parts they need, and looks for orders with no movement (no shipping scan, no status change) beyond a set time. It sends a short daily list with what is wrong and a suggested next step, such as contacting the customer, transferring stock or chasing a carrier.
setup: Read access to stock and order or job data and carrier tracking if relevant. Setup is often several days.
human_checks: A person decides on each fix and approves any customer message.
Stock changes in the system are made by staff.
Thresholds are tuned to avoid false alarms.

examples.scenario: Two customer orders depend on a part with zero stock and no open purchase order; the list suggests ordering and warning the customers.
A delivery has shown no carrier update for six days; a draft message to the customer and a carrier inquiry are prepared.
Three scheduled repairs need a part not yet received, so the dispatcher can reschedule before the technician drives out.

copy_prompt: Each [morning], check stock in [system] against minimums [file], open orders or jobs against the stock or parts they need, and order tracking for anything with no update in [5] days. List problems with a suggested next step for each. Draft customer messages where needed. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Problems surface while there is still time to fix them quietly.

title: Tracking supplier lead times and late deliveries
summary: SI records when orders are placed and received, works out each supplier's real lead time, and flags late deliveries early.
problem: Lead times are guesses based on what the supplier once said. Late deliveries are noticed only when something is missing, and planning uses numbers nobody has checked.
what_si_does: SI logs order dates, promised dates and received dates from purchase orders, confirmations and receiving records. It calculates each supplier's typical lead time and on-time rate over recent orders, flags open orders past their promised date, and drafts a polite chase email.
setup: Purchase order and receiving records, plus supplier emails. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: Chase emails are approved before sending.
Supplier changes are a business decision for the owner.
Lead-time figures are reviewed before they feed into reorder planning.

examples.scenario: Hardware from one supplier now takes about twice as long as the quoted lead time; the reorder plan is updated.
Nursery orders for a spring planting job are past their promised date; a chase email is drafted to the nursery.
Can and label deliveries are tracked so production dates are set around real lead times.
