copy_prompt: From these purchase orders and receiving records [files], calculate each supplier's typical lead time and share of on-time deliveries over the last [6] months. List open orders past their promised date and draft a polite chase email for each. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Planning uses real lead times, and late deliveries get chased before they cause problems.

title: Inventory value and aging report
summary: SI shows how much money is tied up in stock, what has not moved in months, and suggests what to discount, return or stop buying.
problem: Cash gets tied up in items that sit on shelves. Without an aging view, slow items keep getting reordered and dead stock is discovered at year-end counts.
what_si_does: SI combines stock on hand, unit cost and last sale or use date to show inventory value by category and age band (for example, sold in the last 30 days, 31 to 90, over 90, never). It lists the largest pockets of slow stock with options: return to supplier, discount, bundle, or stop reordering.
setup: Stock, cost and sales or usage data. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: The owner decides what to discount or return.
Cost data is checked against supplier invoices.
Seasonal items are marked so they are not flagged out of season.

examples.scenario: Older-model accessories and a few last-season bikes hold a large share of stock value; the report suggests a fall clearance and returning one unopened case.
Fittings for a discontinued fixture line have not moved in a year and are listed for return or write-off review.
Variants in uncommon sizes have not sold in over 90 days; the report suggests stopping reorders on them.

copy_prompt: Using stock on hand [file], unit costs [file] and last sale or use dates [file], show inventory value by [category] and age band: [0-30, 31-90, 91-180, 180+ days, never]. List the [20] largest slow items with options: return, discount, bundle or stop reordering. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Clearer view of where cash is sitting, and better decisions on what not to reorder.

title: Checking customer orders against their PO and payment
summary: Before an order ships or work starts, SI compares the customer's purchase order, your invoice and their payment, and flags any mismatch.
problem: Business customers send purchase orders, then pay by transfer with a reference that may or may not match. Mismatched quantities, prices and amounts cause billing disputes and delays.
what_si_does: SI reads the customer's purchase order, your sales order or invoice, and the payment record or remittance. It checks customer, quantities, prices, totals, tax and payment amount, and lists mismatches. When everything matches it drafts the order confirmation; when it does not, it drafts a clarifying question.
setup: Access to the inbox where purchase orders and remittances arrive, plus invoices and bank or payment records. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A person releases the order or work after reviewing any mismatch.
Confirmation and clarification emails are approved before sending.
Payment records are read-only for SI.

examples.scenario: A school district's purchase order lists a lower unit price than the invoice; the order is held and a clarification drafted.
A restaurant group's payment covers two of three invoices; the remittance is matched and the gap noted.
A corporate client's purchase order is matched to the quote and deposit before the delivery is scheduled.

copy_prompt: For each order in [inbox/folder], compare the customer's purchase order with our invoice [file] and payment record [file]. Check customer, quantities, prices, totals, tax and amount paid. List mismatches. Draft a confirmation for matches and a clarifying question for mismatches. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Billing disputes are caught before the order ships, not after the invoice is overdue.

title: Product and service descriptions from specs, plus catalog cleanup
summary: SI writes consistent descriptions from spec sheets and notes, and cleans up names, categories and details across your catalog, menu or service list.
problem: Descriptions are missing, copied from suppliers, or written in five different styles. Names and categories are inconsistent, which makes things hard to find and harder to sell.
what_si_does: SI reads spec sheets, supplier data or your own notes and writes descriptions in a consistent format and voice: what it is, who it is for, key details, and care or usage notes. It also proposes fixes across the list: consistent naming, missing sizes or details, duplicate entries and wrong categories, as a change sheet for review.
setup: An export of the catalog, menu or service list, spec sheets, and a style example. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A person approves changes before they are applied.
Specs that SI could not confirm are flagged rather than guessed.
Health, safety and performance claims are checked against the source.

examples.scenario: Stone, mulch and soil products get descriptions with coverage per cubic yard and delivery notes, and duplicate listings for the same gravel are merged.
Service descriptions are rewritten consistently with duration, preparation and aftercare, without medical claims.
Product titles are standardized to brand, product, size and color, and missing material details are listed for the owner to fill in.

copy_prompt: Using these spec sheets [files] and this style example [paste], write descriptions for these items [list] with what it is, who it is for, key details and care or usage notes. Then review this catalog export [file] and propose fixes for naming, missing details, duplicates and categories as a change sheet. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: A cleaner, more consistent catalog that is easier for customers to search and staff to maintain.

title: A newsletter drafted from what actually happened
summary: Each week or month SI collects real updates from your calendar, projects, photos and notes, and drafts a newsletter for you to edit.
problem: Newsletters stall because nobody knows what to write. When one does go out, it is generic and late.
what_si_does: SI gathers what actually happened: completed projects, new staff, upcoming events, new services, a seasonal tip, customer questions worth answering. It drafts a short issue in your voice with suggested subject lines and photo spots, and leaves out anything not confirmed.
setup: Access to sources such as the calendar, project tool, shared photo folder or a running notes doc, plus a couple of past issues. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: The owner edits and approves the issue before it is scheduled.
Customer names or photos are used only with permission.
Mailing lists follow opt-in and unsubscribe rules.

examples.scenario: The monthly issue covers two finished homes with photos, a framing update on a new street, and a reminder about the warranty-check schedule.
A seasonal note on ticks, a new vet's introduction, and holiday hours.
Audition dates, a rehearsal photo and volunteer needs for the next show.

copy_prompt: Collect updates for [period] from [calendar, project tool, photo folder, notes doc]. Draft a newsletter in this voice [past issue] with [3-5] short sections, [3] subject-line options and spots for photos. Leave out anything not confirmed in the sources. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Newsletters go out more regularly and reflect the real business.

title: A month of social posts from one source
summary: SI turns one set of updates, photos or a single article into a month of platform-specific posts for you to approve and schedule.
problem: Posting regularly is hard to keep up with. Accounts go quiet for weeks, then get a burst of rushed posts.
what_si_does: From a source you provide (a photo folder, a blog post, notes on upcoming events, past customer questions), SI drafts a calendar of posts suited to each platform, with captions, hashtags where useful, suggested images and posting dates. It varies the mix: work examples, tips, behind-the-scenes, events and offers.
setup: Access to the source material and the scheduling tool. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: Every post is approved before scheduling.
Photos of people are used only with permission.
Offers and prices are checked by the owner.

examples.scenario: Before-and-after photos of five bathrooms become a month of posts with short notes on materials and layout choices.
The weekly specials list and holiday pre-order dates become posts timed to order cutoffs.
A quarterly market letter becomes several short educational posts reviewed for compliance.

copy_prompt: Using [source: photos, article, notes], draft [12] posts for [platforms] over [month], with captions, suggested image and date for each. Mix work examples, tips, behind-the-scenes and events. Keep my voice [examples]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: A steady posting rhythm without the weekly scramble.
caution: Regulated professions (financial, legal, medical) usually have rules for public communications; route posts through whoever handles compliance.

title: One talk, class or article into several pieces
summary: SI turns one long piece, such as a talk, webinar, interview or article, into shorter posts, an email, a handout and short video scripts.
problem: Good long content gets used once. Making shorter versions for other channels takes as long as writing the original.
what_si_does: From a recording or transcript, SI pulls out the strongest points and drafts several pieces: a summary article, an email, a few short social posts, a one-page handout and short video scripts with suggested clip timestamps. Each piece keeps your wording where possible and notes its source.
setup: The source recording or document and a style example. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: The speaker or author approves each piece.
Quotes are checked against the transcript.
Nothing is published without approval.

examples.scenario: A webinar on new leave rules becomes a client alert, an email, three short posts and a one-page summary for HR managers, all reviewed by an attorney.
A long podcast episode becomes short exercise tips and a handout for clients.
The director's annual meeting speech becomes a donor letter and a series of impact posts.

copy_prompt: Here is a transcript of [talk/article]: [file]. Draft a summary article, an email, [5] social posts, a one-page handout and [3] short video scripts with timestamps for clips. Keep my wording where possible. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: More value from each piece of content, with less time spent rewriting it.

title: Refreshing tired web pages and search snippets
summary: SI reviews your key web pages for outdated details, weak titles and missing information, and proposes specific rewrites you approve.
problem: Service and category pages were written years ago. Hours, prices and services are out of date, titles and descriptions in search results are vague, and important questions are not answered.
what_si_does: SI reads your main pages and checks for outdated details, missing basics (service area, hours, how to book), unclear headings, and weak page titles and meta descriptions. It proposes rewrites for each page in a change sheet, and drafts a few short articles that answer common customer questions.
setup: A list of pages, the site editor or a person to apply changes, and the current facts. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: The owner approves every change.
SI does not change live pages without approval.
Facts like prices and services are confirmed by the owner.

examples.scenario: Service pages get clear titles naming the services and towns covered, and a new page answers how often chimneys should be inspected.
Practice-area pages are rewritten in plainer language with a clear consultation process, reviewed by an attorney.
Seasonal category pages are refreshed with current plant availability and planting tips.

copy_prompt: Review these pages [URLs]. For each, list outdated details, missing basics [service area, hours, booking], and weak headings. Propose a new page title, meta description and rewritten sections in a change sheet. Suggest [3] short articles answering common questions [list]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: A website that is current and clearer, which helps both visitors and search results.

title: Checking marketing copy for claims you cannot back up
summary: Before something is published, SI checks the copy against your evidence and flags claims that are unsupported, outdated or risky.
problem: Marketing copy picks up phrases like 'best in town', 'guaranteed' or 'clinically proven' that nobody can support. Old claims stay on the site long after they stopped being true.
what_si_does: SI reads the draft or existing pages and lists each factual claim: superlatives, guarantees, numbers, certifications, results and comparisons. For each it looks for support in the evidence you provide (licenses, certifications, warranty terms, documented results) and labels it supported, unsupported or needs review, with a softer alternative.
setup: The copy to check and a folder of supporting documents. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: The owner or compliance reviewer decides final wording.
SI does not give legal opinions on advertising rules.
Industry-specific rules are checked by the responsible person.

examples.scenario: 'Lifetime warranty' is flagged because the manufacturer warranty has conditions; a clearer phrasing is suggested.
Health benefit claims on product pages are listed for review against what is allowed.
A brochure line about 'guaranteed savings' is flagged and rewritten.

copy_prompt: Review this copy [draft or URLs]. List every factual claim, guarantee, comparison, number or certification. Check each against this evidence [folder] and label it supported, unsupported or needs review. Suggest a supported alternative for each problem claim. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer claims you cannot stand behind, and a cleaner review process before publishing.
caution: Advertising rules vary by industry and place (health, finance and legal services are stricter). SI flags wording; it does not replace review by a lawyer or compliance person.

title: Reviewing and rewriting your automated emails
summary: SI reviews the emails your systems send automatically, such as welcomes, booking confirmations and follow-ups, and drafts clearer replacements.
problem: Automated emails were set up once and forgotten. Some have old details, some are missing entirely, and the tone does not match the business.
what_si_does: SI collects your automated messages (welcome, confirmation, reminder, post-visit or post-purchase, review request, inactive-customer follow-up), checks them for outdated details, gaps and unclear calls to action, and maps which moments have no message at all. It drafts replacements and new messages for approval.
setup: Copies or screenshots of current automated emails and the list of customer journey steps. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: The owner approves every message before it is switched on.
Opt-in and unsubscribe rules are followed.
Changes are tested with a test address first.

examples.scenario: The new-patient welcome email still lists an old address; a replacement is drafted with parking and what to wear.
There is no follow-up after a tour; a short sequence is drafted with a link to book a second visit.
The abandoned-cart email offers a discount the owner no longer gives; a version without it is drafted.

copy_prompt: Here are my automated emails [files or screenshots] and the customer steps [list]. Check each email for outdated details, gaps and unclear calls to action. List steps with no email. Draft replacements and new emails in my voice [example]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Automated messages are accurate and consistent, and gaps in the customer journey are filled.

title: Job postings drafted from a quick description of the role
summary: SI turns a manager's rough notes about a role into a clear job posting, screening questions and a short interview plan.
problem: Job postings get copied from old ones or the internet, with vague duties and requirements that do not match the actual job. The wrong people apply and the right ones skip it.
what_si_does: From the manager's notes or a voice memo, SI drafts a posting with a plain summary, real day-to-day duties, must-have and nice-to-have requirements, schedule, pay range if you share it, and how to apply. It suggests a few job-related screening questions and flags wording that could unintentionally discourage qualified applicants.
setup: Manager notes, past postings and your standard benefits text. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: The hiring manager approves the posting before it is published.
Requirements are checked to be job-related.
Pay transparency and posting rules where you hire are confirmed by a person.

examples.scenario: Notes on a second-year apprentice role become a posting with the license stage, truck and tool details, and on-call expectations stated clearly.
A seasonal tax preparer posting lists software used, busy-season hours and remote options.
A line cook posting lists the stations, shift pattern and what a trial shift involves.

copy_prompt: Here are my notes on a [role]: [paste]. Draft a job posting with a short summary, day-to-day duties, must-have and nice-to-have requirements, schedule, pay range [if provided], and how to apply. Suggest [5] job-related screening questions. Flag any wording that could discourage qualified applicants. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Clearer postings that attract better-matched applicants.
caution: Hiring: employment and anti-discrimination laws apply. Screening criteria must be job-related and applied consistently, SI should never score on protected characteristics, and some places regulate automated hiring tools. A person makes every hiring decision.

title: Summarizing job applications against the role's criteria
summary: SI summarizes each application against the criteria you set for the role, so the hiring manager reads a consistent digest and decides.
problem: A posting brings in dozens or hundreds of applications. Busy managers skim, miss good candidates, and apply different standards on different days.
what_si_does: SI reads each application and summarizes it against the written, job-related criteria: required license or certification, relevant experience, availability, and answers to screening questions. It notes where information is missing and groups applications into meets criteria, partly meets, and does not show the requirement, with the reason. It does not reject anyone; the manager reviews.
setup: The role's written criteria, access to applications from the job board or applicant tracker. Setup is often a day or two per role type.
human_checks: A person reviews every application group and makes all decisions.
SI ignores names, photos, ages and other protected characteristics in its summaries.
Criteria and outcomes are reviewed periodically for consistency and fairness.

examples.scenario: Caregiver applications are summarized by certification, driving availability and weekend availability, with missing certification dates noted.
Journeyman applicants are summarized by license status and type of work, and the owner calls the ones who meet the requirements.
Teaching applications are summarized by subject certification and grade-level experience for the principal.

copy_prompt: Here are the written criteria for [role]: [paste]. Summarize each application in [folder/applicant tracker] against those criteria only, ignoring names, photos, age and other personal characteristics. Group them into meets, partly meets and does not show the requirement, with a one-line reason and any missing information. Do not reject anyone. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Managers spend their time on the most relevant applicants, with a consistent first read.
caution: Hiring: employment and anti-discrimination laws apply. Screening criteria must be job-related and applied consistently, SI should never score on protected characteristics, and some places regulate automated hiring tools. A person makes every hiring decision.

title: Interview scheduling and a consistent question kit
summary: SI coordinates interview times with candidates and interviewers, and prepares a consistent question set and scoring sheet for each role.
problem: Interviews take a string of emails to schedule. Each interviewer asks different questions, which makes candidates hard to compare.
what_si_does: SI drafts messages to shortlisted candidates offering times that work for the interviewers, books confirmed slots, and sends reminders. For each role it prepares a short kit: the same job-related questions for every candidate, what a good answer covers, and a simple scoring sheet for interviewers to fill in.
setup: Calendar access for interviewers, candidate contacts and the role's criteria. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: Candidate messages are approved before sending.
The hiring manager approves the questions.
Interview notes and scores are kept with access limited to the hiring team.

examples.scenario: Three hygienist candidates are offered times around the dentist's patient schedule, and the kit covers patient communication and sterilization procedures.
A designer candidate gets times with two interviewers and a short portfolio review structure.
Program coordinator interviews use the same questions for all candidates, including board members on the panel.

copy_prompt: For [role], draft messages to these candidates [list] offering [3] times that fit [interviewers' calendars]. Prepare an interview kit with [6] job-related questions, what a strong answer covers, and a scoring sheet. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Less scheduling back-and-forth and fairer, easier comparisons between candidates.
caution: Hiring: employment and anti-discrimination laws apply. Screening criteria must be job-related and applied consistently, SI should never score on protected characteristics, and some places regulate automated hiring tools. A person makes every hiring decision.

title: A new-hire onboarding checklist that actually gets followed
summary: SI builds a role-specific onboarding plan, sends reminders to whoever owns each step, and tracks what is done.
problem: First weeks are improvised. Accounts are not ready, paperwork is chased late, and training depends on who has time that day.
what_si_does: From your standard onboarding steps and the role, SI builds a dated checklist: paperwork, accounts and keys, equipment, introductions, training sessions and first-month check-ins, each with an owner. It sends reminders to owners before due dates, drafts a welcome email with first-day details, and reports what is still open.
setup: Your onboarding steps, role templates, and the tools for tasks and email. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: HR or the manager approves the plan and any messages to the new hire.
Personal documents are handled in your HR system, not in chat or email.
Required legal paperwork is confirmed by the responsible person.

examples.scenario: A new leasing agent's plan includes software logins, a ride-along with a senior agent and a fair-housing training session in week one.
A new prep cook gets food-safety training, a station walkthrough and uniform sizing before the first shift.
A new paralegal's accounts, conflict-system training and a meeting with each practice group are scheduled.

copy_prompt: Using our onboarding steps [paste] and this role [description], build a dated checklist for [name] starting [date], with an owner for each step. Draft a welcome email with first-day details. Set reminders for owners [2] days before each step. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: New hires get a steadier start, and fewer steps are missed.

title: An internal helper that answers staff questions from your own documents
summary: SI answers staff questions about procedures, policies, products and prices from your own documents, and says where it found the answer.
problem: Staff interrupt the owner or senior people with the same questions all day. The answers exist in a handbook, price sheet or old email, but nobody can find them quickly.
what_si_does: SI is connected to an approved set of internal documents: the handbook, procedures, price lists, spec sheets and FAQs. Staff ask in chat, and SI answers with a short reply and a link to the source. When the documents do not cover a question, it says so and routes the question to the right person, and the gap is logged so the documents can be updated.
setup: A tidy set of approved documents and a chat tool. Setup is often one to two weeks, mostly organizing the documents.
human_checks: Only approved documents are used, and sources are always shown.
Questions about pay, discipline or personal matters go to a person.
Document owners review the gap log monthly.

examples.scenario: Counter staff ask which filters fit a given unit and get the answer with a link to the cross-reference sheet.
Front-desk staff check the procedure for a new patient's insurance verification and get the steps from the office manual.
Store staff check the holiday return policy and price-match rules.

copy_prompt: Answer staff questions using only these documents [folder]. Give a short answer and link the source. If the documents do not cover it, say so and suggest who to ask [contacts]. Keep a log of unanswered questions. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer interruptions for senior staff, and documents that improve as gaps are found.

title: Tracking staff licenses, certifications and training renewals
summary: SI keeps one list of staff licenses, certifications and required training with expiry dates, and reminds people well before anything lapses.
problem: Licenses, certifications and required trainings expire on different dates. A lapse can mean someone cannot work, or a problem at an inspection or audit.
what_si_does: SI reads certificates and records from a shared folder or HR system, builds a list of each person's credentials with issue and expiry dates, and sends reminders to the person and their manager ahead of each expiry. It flags anyone scheduled for work that requires a credential they do not currently hold.
setup: Copies of certificates or HR records, and the list of required credentials per role. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A manager confirms dates against the original documents.
Scheduling decisions about uncertified staff are made by a person.
Credential records are kept with access limited to managers.

examples.scenario: Electrician licenses, lift certifications and safety training are tracked, with a reminder to renew a lift card before a job that needs it.
CPR and first-aid certifications and background-check renewals are tracked for every staff member.
Nursing licenses and required annual trainings are tracked for each caregiver.

copy_prompt: From these certificates and records [folder], build a list of each person's licenses, certifications and trainings with issue and expiry dates. Compare with required credentials per role [file]. Draft reminders [60] and [14] days before expiry, and flag anyone scheduled for work needing a credential they lack. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer surprise lapses and fewer scrambles before inspections.

title: Reviewing timesheets and time off before payroll
summary: Before each payroll run, SI checks timesheets against schedules and time-off records and lists anything that looks wrong for a person to fix.
problem: Payroll errors come from missed punches, unapproved overtime and time off that was never recorded. They are found after the paychecks, which is awkward for everyone.
what_si_does: SI compares timesheets with the schedule, approved time-off requests and job or project codes. It lists missing punches, unusually long shifts, overtime without approval, time off taken but not recorded, and hours coded to the wrong job. It prepares a summary for the payroll person. It does not run payroll or approve hours.
setup: Exports from time tracking, scheduling and time-off records. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A manager resolves each flagged item with the employee.
Payroll is run and approved by a person.
Wage-and-hour rules are the owner's or payroll provider's responsibility.

examples.scenario: Two crew members are missing clock-outs on the same day, and overtime on a Saturday job was not approved.
A server's paid sick day was taken but not recorded, and a cook's hours exceed the schedule by a full shift.
Hours coded to a closed project are flagged before they are billed or paid.

copy_prompt: Compare these timesheets [export] with the schedule [export], approved time off [export] and job codes [list] for [pay period]. List missing punches, shifts over [12] hours, unapproved overtime, unrecorded time off and miscoded hours. Prepare a summary for payroll. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer payroll corrections after the fact.
caution: Payroll and wage rules are regulated. SI only flags issues; payroll decisions and tax filings stay with the owner, payroll provider or accountant.

title: A first read of contracts for the terms that matter
summary: SI highlights dates, renewal terms, payment terms and unusual clauses in contracts so you know what to ask your lawyer or the other side.
problem: Contracts, leases and vendor agreements get signed after a skim. Auto-renewals, notice periods, liability terms and penalties come as surprises later.
what_si_does: SI reads the contract and produces a plain summary: parties, term, renewal and notice, payment terms, termination, liability and insurance requirements, exclusivity, and anything that differs from your usual terms or a checklist you provide. It lists questions to raise. It does not say whether a clause is acceptable or enforceable.
setup: The contract and, ideally, a checklist of terms you care about or a standard version to compare against. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: A lawyer reviews anything significant before signing.
SI's summary is checked against the actual text.
SI never signs, accepts or sends contracts.

examples.scenario: A new commercial lease summary highlights a personal guarantee, a percentage-rent clause and the required notice to renew.
A client's master services agreement is compared with the agency's standard terms, flagging an unlimited revision clause and payment at 90 days.
A grant agreement's reporting deadlines and restrictions on spending are pulled into a calendar and summary.

copy_prompt: Read this contract [file]. Summarize parties, term, renewal and notice, payment, termination, liability, insurance, exclusivity and any unusual clauses. Compare it with [my checklist or standard terms] and list differences and questions for my lawyer. Do not give a legal opinion. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: You go into contract discussions knowing which terms matter, and legal review time goes to the important questions.
caution: Legal: this is an organizing aid, not legal advice. SI may miss or misread terms. Have a qualified lawyer review contracts that matter.

title: Filling routine forms from saved company details
summary: SI fills vendor setup forms, applications, permits and questionnaires from a saved set of company details, and stops before anything is submitted.
problem: The same information (legal name, tax ID, insurance details, addresses, contacts) is typed into form after form. Errors creep in, and forms sit unfinished.
what_si_does: SI keeps a profile of verified company details and documents (certificate of insurance, licenses, standard answers). For each new form, it fills what it can, lists fields it could not answer, and attaches the right documents. It stops before signing or submitting, and leaves the finished draft for review.
setup: A verified company profile and document folder. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: A person checks and submits every form.
Sensitive identifiers are stored securely and shared only where required.
SI never signs on anyone's behalf.

examples.scenario: A general contractor's subcontractor packet is filled with license numbers, insurance limits and safety program answers, with two questions left for the owner.
A grocery distributor's vendor setup form is completed and the food-safety certificate attached.
Venue permit applications for an outdoor event are pre-filled from the event details.

copy_prompt: Using my company profile [file] and documents [folder], fill out this form [file or link]. List any fields you could not complete and attach the matching documents. Do not sign or submit. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Forms are completed faster and more consistently, with fewer errors.
caution: Tax and government forms: SI fills in information you have already verified; it does not decide tax classifications or legal answers. Confirm anything you are unsure of with your accountant or lawyer.

title: Short briefs from long documents
summary: SI reads long documents such as regulations, bid packages, reports or board packets and writes a short brief with what matters to you and what to do next.
problem: Important documents are long and dense, and reading them carefully takes time nobody has. Key requirements and deadlines get missed.
what_si_does: SI reads the document and writes a brief: what it is, the key points, requirements or decisions that affect you, deadlines, and open questions, with page references for each point so you can check the source.
setup: The document and a short description of what you care about. Setup is minimal.
human_checks: Important points are checked against the page references.
Interpretations of rules are confirmed by a qualified person.
SI flags uncertainty rather than guessing.

examples.scenario: A large bid package becomes a brief with scope, submission deadline, bonding and insurance requirements and pre-bid meeting date, with page numbers.
A city's new food-service regulations are summarized with what changes for kitchens and when it takes effect.
A long board packet becomes a two-page brief with the votes coming up and the questions worth asking.

copy_prompt: Read this document [file]. I am [role] at [organization] and care about [topics]. Write a brief with key points, requirements affecting us, deadlines and open questions, with page references for each. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Long documents get a careful first read quickly, and the important parts are easier to find.
caution: When the document is a regulation, contract or legal notice, the brief is not legal advice; confirm interpretations with a qualified professional.

title: Drafting bids, RFP responses and grant applications from past answers
summary: SI drafts responses to bids, RFPs and grant applications from your past submissions and documents, and lists what still needs a human answer.
problem: Each application asks similar questions in different words. Teams rewrite the same answers from scratch, under deadline, and miss requirements.
what_si_does: SI reads the request, builds a checklist of every required section, attachment and format rule, and drafts answers by drawing on past submissions, capability statements and project summaries. It marks each answer as reused, adapted or new, and lists questions with no good source answer. It also prepares a submission checklist with the deadline.
setup: A folder of past submissions, capability statements, bios and project summaries. Setup is often a few days to organize the library.
human_checks: A person reviews every answer and all budget figures.
Claims about past work are checked against records.
Submission is done by a person.

examples.scenario: A foundation grant application is drafted from last year's proposal and program reports, with the new evaluation section flagged as needing input.
A city's request for proposals gets a compliance checklist and draft answers from previous public-sector bids.
A qualifications package is assembled with relevant project sheets and team resumes.

copy_prompt: Read this request [file]. Build a checklist of required sections, attachments, formats and the deadline. Draft answers using these past submissions and documents [folder], marking each as reused, adapted or new. List questions with no good source. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Applications start from a solid draft, and requirements are less likely to be missed.

title: Pulling data out of PDFs and scans, and filing them
summary: SI reads PDFs, scans and photos, extracts the fields you need into a spreadsheet, and renames and files the documents consistently.
problem: Information is trapped in PDFs, scans and phone photos: statements, forms, delivery notes, certificates. Someone retypes it, and the files end up in a messy downloads folder.
what_si_does: SI reads each document, extracts the fields you specify (dates, names, amounts, reference numbers, line items), and writes them to a spreadsheet with a link to the source file. It renames files with a consistent pattern and moves them into the right folders, and lists documents it could not read clearly.
setup: A source folder, the list of fields, and a naming pattern. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: Extracted values are spot-checked against the documents.
Unreadable or uncertain fields are flagged, not guessed.
Original files are kept unchanged.

examples.scenario: A year of scanned utility bills across buildings becomes a sheet of usage and cost by building and month.
Proof-of-delivery scans are renamed by load number and the delivery dates extracted for billing.
Faxed referral forms are filed by referring practice and the key referral details logged for the scheduling team.

copy_prompt: For each document in [folder], extract [fields] into [sheet] with a link to the file. Rename each file as [pattern] and move it to [folder rules]. List any document or field you could not read clearly. Do not change the original contents. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Less retyping, and documents that can actually be found later.
caution: Medical records and other personal data must be handled under the privacy rules that apply to you (for example HIPAA). Use approved, secure tools only.

title: Comparing vendors, tools or options in one decision sheet
summary: SI researches the options for a purchase or decision and lays them out side by side against your requirements, with sources.
problem: Choosing a new supplier, software tool or service provider means reading websites, quotes and reviews that never compare the same things. Decisions end up based on whoever had the best sales call.
what_si_does: From your requirements and the options you are considering, SI collects published information and the quotes you have received, and builds a comparison sheet: price and terms, features against requirements, contract length, support, and open questions for each vendor. It flags where information is missing or based only on the vendor's own claims.
setup: Your requirements and the quotes or vendor names. Setup is minimal.
human_checks: The owner makes the decision.
Facts are linked to sources and checked before relying on them.
Questions for vendors are sent by a person.

examples.scenario: Three practice-management systems are compared on scheduling, imaging integration, monthly cost, data migration and contract length.
Quotes for two truck lease offers are compared on mileage limits, maintenance and early termination.
Three insurance quotes are compared on coverage limits and exclusions, with questions for the broker.

copy_prompt: I need to choose [type of vendor or tool]. My requirements are [list]. Compare these options [names, quotes, links] side by side on price, terms, requirements met, contract length and support. Link sources and flag anything missing or based only on vendor claims. List questions to ask each vendor. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Decisions rest on a clear comparison rather than a sales pitch.

title: Handing recurring web-portal chores to SI
summary: SI works through recurring tasks in web portals, such as downloading statements, checking statuses and entering routine data, and stops before any final step.
problem: Admin work is full of small portal tasks: download this month's statements from six sites, check claim or permit status, update the same info in three places. Each is quick, together they eat hours.
what_si_does: With access you grant, SI logs into the portals you list, follows the written steps for each chore, downloads files into the right folders, records statuses in a sheet, and fills routine data entries. Before any step that submits, pays, accepts terms or changes account settings, it stops and asks.
setup: A written list of chores and steps, and access set up the way you choose (preferably with limited-permission user accounts). Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: SI stops before any submit, payment, signature or setting change.
Access uses limited-permission accounts where possible, and passwords are not shared in chat.
A person spot-checks downloads and entries.

examples.scenario: On the first business day, SI downloads utility and bank statements from each portal and files them by property.
SI checks the status of a list of insurance claims in payer portals and records which need follow-up.
Permit status is checked weekly on the town portals for each active job and logged in the job sheet.

copy_prompt: Do these portal chores [list with steps] for [period]. Download files into [folders] with names [pattern], record statuses in [sheet], and enter this routine data [file]. Stop before any step that submits, pays, signs, accepts terms or changes settings. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Routine portal work gets done on schedule without someone setting aside hours for it.

title: A weekly announcements email for members
summary: SI gathers the week's events, schedule changes and notices from your calendar and contributors, and drafts the members' email for approval.
problem: The weekly email depends on one volunteer or staff member collecting items from everyone by text and email. Items arrive late, details are wrong, and the email goes out late or not at all.
what_si_does: SI collects items from a submission form, the shared calendar and forwarded emails, checks dates and times against the calendar, and drafts the email in your usual layout: this week's schedule, upcoming events, notices, volunteer needs and celebrations. It lists items with missing details for the editor.
setup: A submission form, calendar access and a past issue as a template. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: The editor or administrator approves the email before it goes out.
Personal news (illness, bereavement) is included only with permission.
Mailing lists follow subscribe and unsubscribe rules.

examples.scenario: Service times for the week, a guest speaker, the kiddush sponsor and a volunteer call for the holiday are pulled into the Thursday email.
Pool hours, a landscaping schedule and the next board meeting go into the weekly bulletin.
Game schedule changes, field closures and picture-day details are gathered from coaches.

copy_prompt: Collect items for [week] from [submission form, calendar, forwarded emails]. Check dates and times against [calendar]. Draft the members' email in this layout [past issue] with schedule, events, notices, volunteer needs and celebrations. List items with missing details. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: The weekly email goes out on time with fewer errors and less chasing.

title: Donation thank-yous and acknowledgment letters
summary: SI drafts personal thank-you letters and acknowledgment receipts from donation records, using wording your accountant has approved.
problem: Thank-yous go out weeks late or not at all. Acknowledgment letters need specific details, and preparing them one by one is slow.
what_si_does: SI reads new donations from your donor system or payment exports, drafts a thank-you that mentions the gift and any designation, and prepares an acknowledgment with the details your approved template requires. It flags gifts that need special handling, such as large gifts, in-kind gifts or gifts in memory of someone, and compiles year-end summaries per donor.
setup: Donation records and an acknowledgment template approved by your accountant. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: A person reviews and sends every letter.
Acknowledgment wording is approved by the organization's accountant.
Large, in-kind and memorial gifts are handled personally.

examples.scenario: Gifts from a holiday drive get thank-yous within the week, with in-kind food donations listed by description rather than value.
Monthly donors get a short note about the animals adopted that month, and year-end summaries are prepared in January.
Sponsors of a show get a thank-you naming the production and their program listing.

copy_prompt: For donations in [export] since [date], draft a thank-you for each that mentions the gift and designation, using this tone [example]. Prepare acknowledgments using this approved template [file]. Flag gifts over [amount], in-kind gifts and memorial gifts. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Donors are thanked promptly and accurately.
caution: Tax: acknowledgment requirements depend on where you are and the type of gift. Use wording approved by your accountant; SI does not value in-kind gifts or advise donors on deductions.

title: Volunteer sign-ups, reminders and gap filling
summary: SI organizes volunteer sign-ups, sends reminders, spots unfilled shifts, and drafts targeted asks to people likely to help.
problem: Volunteer coordination runs on group texts and memory. Shifts go unfilled until the last minute, and the same few people get asked every time.
what_si_does: SI keeps the sign-up sheet current from form responses and replies, sends reminders before each shift, and lists unfilled slots. For gaps, it drafts a short ask to volunteers who have helped with that kind of task before but have not been asked recently.
setup: A sign-up form or sheet, volunteer contacts and past participation. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: The coordinator approves messages to volunteers.
Volunteers who opted out are not contacted.
Roles that need background checks are filled only by cleared volunteers.

examples.scenario: Weekday lunch shifts are tracked, and a Wednesday gap gets an ask to three people who have done that shift before.
Build-day volunteers get reminders with the site address and what to wear.
Book-fair shifts are filled and parents get reminders the evening before.

copy_prompt: Using sign-ups [sheet/form] and volunteer history [file], list unfilled shifts for [period]. Draft reminders for confirmed volunteers [1] day before. For each gap, draft a short ask to [3] volunteers who have done similar shifts and have not been asked in [30] days. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Fewer last-minute gaps, and the volunteer load is spread more evenly.

title: Event registration, seating and reminders
summary: SI combines registrations and payments, flags unpaid or duplicate entries, drafts seating and name tags, and sends approved reminders.
problem: Event logistics live in several places: a form, a payment tool, a spreadsheet and someone's notes. The last week before the event is frantic, and details slip.
what_si_does: SI merges registrations and payments, lists unpaid and duplicate entries, and produces headcounts, dietary lists and name tags. It drafts seating by your rules (households together, sponsors near the front), drafts reminder and logistics emails, and produces the final count for the caterer or venue.
setup: Registration and payment exports, seating rules and message templates. Setup is often a few days before the event.
human_checks: The organizer approves seating and every message.
Payment follow-ups are sent by a person.
Final counts to the caterer or venue are confirmed by a person.

examples.scenario: The annual dinner's registrations are reconciled with payments, and members registered twice through two links are merged.
A charity golf outing's foursomes are drafted and sponsor signage is listed.
A reunion's dietary list and name tags are produced, with reminders sent three days before.

copy_prompt: Combine these registrations [file] and payments [file] for [event]. List unpaid and duplicate entries, draft seating for [tables] tables of [10] using these rules [paste], and produce dietary and name-tag lists. Draft a reminder email for [3] days before. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Event logistics are calmer in the final week, and fewer details slip.

title: Membership renewals and a clean member list
summary: SI tracks renewal dates, drafts reminders, and cleans up the member list by merging duplicates and flagging outdated contact details.
problem: Renewals depend on someone remembering to send reminders. The member list has duplicates, old emails and households listed three ways.
what_si_does: SI reads the member list and payment records, lists members due to renew or lapsed, drafts reminders in a friendly sequence, and proposes cleanup: merging duplicates, flagging bounced emails, and standardizing names and households. Lapsed members who were active get a personal-style note for a board member to send.
setup: Member list and payment exports, and your renewal schedule. Setup is often a few days.
human_checks: Merges and deletions are confirmed by a person.
Reminders are approved before sending.
Members with hardship arrangements are handled personally.

examples.scenario: Families due to renew in March get reminders, and households listed under two parents' names are merged.
Lapsed member companies are listed with their last event attended, for a board member to call.
Bounced email addresses are flagged ahead of the spring renewal mailing.

copy_prompt: Using the member list [file] and payments [file], list members due to renew in [period] and those lapsed. Draft a reminder sequence [timing]. Propose merges for likely duplicates, flag bounced or missing emails, and standardize household names. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: More renewals happen on time, and the member list is one you can trust.

title: Session notes into progress updates for families or clients
summary: After each session or class, SI turns the instructor's quick notes into a short, consistent progress update for the parent or client to receive.
problem: Instructors and coaches jot notes but rarely have time to write updates. Families or clients hear little until there is a problem, and the updates that do go out vary wildly.
what_si_does: SI takes the instructor's notes or voice memo and writes a short update in a consistent format: what was covered, what went well, what to practice, and what is next. It keeps a running record per learner so trends are visible, and flags notes that suggest a concern for the instructor to handle personally.
setup: A simple notes form or voice memo path, a template, and contacts. Setup is often a day or two.
human_checks: The instructor approves each update before it is sent.
Concerns are communicated personally, not by template.
Notes about minors are stored with limited access.

examples.scenario: A math tutor's two-line note becomes a parent update on fractions practice and next week's focus.
Lesson notes become a weekly message with the pieces to practice and a tip for the tricky passage.
Each lesson produces a short summary of skills covered and what to practice before the road test.

copy_prompt: Turn these session notes [paste] for [learner] into a short update for [parent/client] with what was covered, what went well, what to practice and what is next, using this template [example]. Flag any note that suggests a concern. Add it to the running record [file]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Families and clients stay informed, and instructors spend less time writing.
caution: If sessions are therapy, counseling or medical in nature, notes are protected health information and need privacy-compliant tools and a clinician's review.

title: Lesson plans, quizzes and training materials for instructors
summary: SI drafts lesson plans, quizzes, handouts and first-pass feedback from your curriculum or materials, for the instructor to review and adapt.
problem: Instructors, trainers and teachers spend evenings building plans and quizzes from scratch. Feedback on written work is slow because there is so much of it.
what_si_does: From your curriculum, textbook pages or training manual, SI drafts a lesson or session plan with goals, activities, timing and a short check for understanding. It creates quizzes at different levels with answer keys, and drafts first-pass feedback on written work against a rubric, which the instructor edits.
setup: The source materials, a rubric if relevant, and examples of the format you use. Setup is minimal.
human_checks: The instructor reviews every plan, quiz and piece of feedback.
Grades are assigned by the instructor, not SI.
Student work is handled under the program's privacy policy.

examples.scenario: A volunteer tutor gets a session plan and a short reading check built around a job-application form.
A forklift-safety manual becomes a session outline and a quiz for new warehouse workers.
A science unit gets a lab plan, two quiz versions and draft feedback on lab reports against the rubric.

copy_prompt: Using these materials [files] and this format [example], draft a [length] session plan for [audience] with goals, activities, timing and a check for understanding. Create a [10]-question quiz with an answer key at [level]. Draft feedback on these submissions [files] against this rubric [file]. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Preparation takes less of the instructor's own time, and feedback gets back to learners sooner.

title: Board packets and minutes for volunteer boards
summary: SI assembles the board packet from committee reports and financials, drafts the agenda, and turns meeting notes into draft minutes for the secretary.
problem: Volunteer boards run on late reports and a packet assembled the night before. Minutes are written weeks later from memory.
what_si_does: SI collects committee reports, the treasurer's summary and any proposals from a shared folder, flags what is missing, and assembles a packet with an agenda and a one-page summary of decisions needed. After the meeting, it drafts minutes from notes or a transcript, listing motions, votes and action items.
setup: A shared folder, a past packet and minutes as templates. Setup is often a day.
human_checks: The chair approves the agenda and packet.
The secretary reviews and finalizes the minutes before approval by the board.
Confidential matters are handled outside the shared packet.

examples.scenario: Packet includes the manager's report, a roof bid comparison and the reserve fund summary, with a note that the landscaping committee report is missing.
Minutes from the monthly meeting list the vote on new member-owner discounts and the follow-up tasks.
The fall packet includes the fundraiser results and the budget for the spring events.

copy_prompt: Gather reports from [folder] for the [date] board meeting. List what is missing, draft an agenda using [past agenda], and write a one-page summary of decisions needed. After the meeting, draft minutes from these notes [paste] with motions, votes and action items. Pause and show me before sending, submitting, posting or changing anything.
effect: Board members arrive prepared, and minutes are ready while the meeting is still fresh.
caution: Minutes can be legal records for some organizations; the secretary and board should approve the final version, and recording requires participants' consent.
